verifications.claim: The 25th Amendment was ratified in 1967 following the JFK assassination.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The 25th Amendment was added to the Constitution in 1967, after the assassination of John F. Kennedy'; R3: 'Ratified in 1967'; R7: 'Amendment Twenty-five ... was ratified on February 10, 1967 ... the assassination of President John F. Kennedy in 1963 which finally pushed Congress'; R9: 'ratified by the states on June 10, 1967 ... Following President John F. Kennedy’s assassination'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state ratification in 1967 and link it to JFK's 1963 assassination as the catalyst.

verifications.claim: Under Section 1 of the 25th Amendment, if the President is removed, dies, or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Section 1 In case of the removal of the President from office or of his death or resignation, the Vice President shall become President'; identical in R6, R7, R8; R3: 'Section 1 ... if the President dies, resigns, or is removed ... the Vice President "shall become President"'
verifications.reasoning: Exact wording of Section 1 quoted in multiple constitutional texts.

verifications.claim: Under Section 2 of the 25th Amendment, the President nominates a new Vice President, confirmed by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Section 2 Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President, the President shall nominate a Vice President who shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress'; identical in R6, R7, R8; R3: 'Section 2 requires the President to nominate a new Vice President ... after confirmation by a majority vote in each chamber of Congress'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to Section 2 text and explanations.

verifications.claim: Under Section 3 of the 25th Amendment, the President declares in writing an inability to serve, making the Vice President Acting President until a written declaration to the contrary is submitted.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Section 3 Whenever the President transmits ... his written declaration that he is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, and until he transmits to them a written declaration to the contrary, such powers and duties shall be discharged by the Vice President as Acting President'; identical in R6, R7, R8; R3: 'Section 3 allows ... by sending a written declaration ... the Vice President serves as Acting President ... until the President communicates that he is again able'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote and paraphrase of Section 3 procedures.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet can declare the President incapacitated, immediately making the VP Acting President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Section 4 Whenever the Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive departments ... their written declaration that the President is unable to discharge ... the Vice President shall immediately assume ... as Acting President'; identical in R6, R7, R8; R3: 'Section 4 ... the Vice President and a majority of the "principal officers ... Cabinet" ... the Vice President immediately assumes ... as Acting President'
verifications.reasoning: Exact constitutional language specifies VP and Cabinet majority declaration leads to immediate Acting President.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, if the President disputes this, Congress decides the issue.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Thereafter, when the President transmits ... he shall resume ... unless the Vice President and a majority ... transmit within four days ... Thereupon Congress shall decide the issue'; identical in R6, R7, R8; R3: 'If the President subsequently declares ... unless ... transmit a contrary ... Congress must assemble ... to determine'; R1: 'The president can challenge this by writing to Congress. But if ... then Congress steps in and votes'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail the dispute process where Congress assembles and votes if VP/Cabinet counters President's declaration.

verifications.claim: In 1973, Gerald Ford was nominated as Vice President by Richard Nixon after Spiro Agnew resigned.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: '1973 when President Richard Nixon nominated Congressman Gerald R. Ford to fill the vacancy left by Vice President Spiro Agnew's resignation'; R3: 'Section 2 ... Vice President Spiro T. Agnew’s ... resignations'; R7: 'Gerald Ford replacing Vice President Spiro Agnew after his resignation in 1973'; R9: 'In 1973, Vice President Spiro Agnew resigned ... Nixon nominated Representative Gerald R. Ford'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm exact events and year.

verifications.claim: In 1974, Gerald Ford became President following Richard Nixon's resignation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'In 1974, Section 1 resulted in Vice President Gerald Ford’s succession to the presidency when President Richard Nixon resigned'; R5: 'Vice President Ford became President after Nixon resigned'; R8: 'In 1974 ... Gerald Ford’s succession ... Richard Nixon resigned'; R9: 'Following Nixon’s resignation in 1974, Ford became President'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm 1974 succession due to Nixon's resignation.

verifications.claim: In 1974, Nelson Rockefeller was appointed Vice President by Ford.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R9: 'President Ford then used the 25th Amendment to nominate New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller as his vice president' (after 1974 Nixon resignation); R5: 'In less than a year [after 1973 Ford nomination], the 25th Amendment was used again when Vice President Ford became President after Nixon resigned' (implying Rockefeller in 1974); R3: 'Section 2 ... invoked twice during the 1970s ... Agnew’s and ... Nixon’s resignations (President Nixon's resignation occasioned the use of Section 2 because Vice President Gerald Ford succeeded Nixon)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Rockefeller's nomination/confirmation in late 1974 following Ford's ascension.

verifications.claim: Presidents Reagan (1985), G.W. Bush (2002, 2007), and Biden (2021) used the 25th Amendment for temporary transfers during medical procedures requiring anesthesia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'The 25th Amendment was notably utilized by Presidents Reagan (1985), G.W. Bush (2002, 2007), and Biden (2021) for procedures requiring anesthesia'; R9: 'President Ronald Reagan used Section 3 ... in 1985 ... President George W. Bush later used ... twice for medical procedures. President Joe Biden also used it for a procedure'
verifications.reasoning: R5 matches exactly; R9 confirms with matching years and context of anesthesia/surgery.

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been used.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Section 4, which has never been invoked'; R5: 'Section 4 has never been used'; R8: 'Section 4, which has never been invoked'; R1: 'the 25th Amendment has never been used to remove a sitting president' (context Section 4); R2: 'The 25th Amendment has never been used to remove a sitting president'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Section 4 has never been invoked/used.
